newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela approves 11.2 trln bolivar budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela approves 11.2 trln bolivar budget plan.

text.p: Venezuela's cabinet of ministers approved Wednesday an 11.2 trillion bolivar ($23.3 billion) budget proposal for 1998, up from 10.2 trillion bolivars in 1997, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
"The budget proposal law for 1998 was approved. It is 11.24 trillion bolivars," Matos told a news conference at Miraflores presidential palace.
Matos said the 1998 budget proposal was based on a government forecast of five percent economic growth and a 15 percent inflation rate.
The government has forecast economic growth of four percent and set a target of 30 to 35 percent inflation for 1997.
The budget was based on an average exchange rate for 1998 of 524 bolivars per dollar, Matos added, correcting his earlier statement that the average assumed rate was 490 bolivars per dollar.
Venezuela's exchange rate closed at 484.00/485.00 bolivars per dollar Tuesday.

The budget was also based on an average export price for Venezuela's basket of crude and products of $15.50 per barrel. The basket of crude and products has averaged $17.66 per barrel so far this year.

Matos said ordinary tax revenues from oil and non-oil activities would account for 9.6 trillion bolivars of 1998 revenues, with extraordinary revenues of 1.6 trillion bolivars coming largely from an 800 billion bolivar dividend from state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA)
"The income side does not include any privatization revenues," he said.
